tasks.short: Monitor the use and status of medical and pharmaceutical supplies.

steps.what: Count medical and pharmaceutical supplies still in the cabinet.
Drop the recopied use list for those pharmaceutical supplies.
Flag supplies whose on-hand count sits below the pharmacist par.
Decide the status of supplies that are short or expired.
Check that supply status against the cabinet count.
Send the confirmed supply status to the pharmacy.
Tell the clinic which pharmaceutical supplies are short today.

tasks.design: The nurse still counts the cabinet, decides the status, and tells the clinic. {OTHER}, the clinic supply record, keeps that count once, so the office recopy of use stops, and it flags only items under the pharmacist's stored par. After she confirms the list, {EMAIL} sends that status to the pharmacy. The message is not a prescription.
tasks.previous_blocker: The count and the use list were copied onto a sheet, and the par sat on a card or in memory, so status was a hand comparison.
tasks.enabler_now: One count entry and a stored par quantity make the below-par flag and the pharmacy message ordinary rules.
tasks.still_hard: Seeing damage, judging what today's clinics need, and the cabinet count itself.
tasks.human_edge: She sees opened packs, wrong labels, and whether today's patients can still be treated.

ambition.what: Every counted supply is flagged against par the same day, including items nobody remembered to mention.

tasks.altitude: She still owns the cabinet count and the status decision. The week loses the second copy of use and the hand comparison. The pharmacy hears only the list she confirmed.

reach.task: Issue clinic supplies against the existing par
reach.learn: The message is a confirmed count against the current par, not a prescription and not a new par.

reach.task: Plan today's clinics around short supplies
reach.learn: Use the shortage she states in person. An unconfirmed flag is not a status.

evidence.claim: A clinic stock status is the count on hand compared with a par quantity set for that item.
A prescription comes from a named practitioner.

assumptions: The on-hand count and the damage note are produced in s1, which stays at remaining 100. The design does not shorten the cabinet count or the noticing of damage.

Par contract, fields item code, par quantity and unit. Producer is the pharmacist when the item is added to the clinic list, stored in the clinic supply record. That capture is not this task and is not counted as saved. Fallback is the shelf par card: the below-par list stays blank and she compares by hand.

Use-log contract, fields item code, quantity and date. Producer is the nurse who issued or administered the supply, written on the administration record at that time. That capture is another task, not saved here. Fallback: she still writes use from memory, and the recopied list is not dropped.

s3 only compares her count with that par. s6 sends only items she marked in the status decision and confirmed in s5. The message is not a prescription and not a purchase order. The pharmacist decides what to issue.
A witness count, where national rules require one for a controlled supply, stays inside s1 at full time. The status is not a score of who used stock.
The 0.6 hour per 100 baseline hours is correcting an item code when the cabinet label and the supply record disagree.
unknowns: Whether par quantities in this clinic already sit in a supply record or only on a shelf card.
Whether national rules require a second person to count controlled pharmaceutical supplies here.
research_questions: Which pharmaceutical supplies in this clinic are controlled and need a second signature on the count?

already_counted.description: Confirming each flagged supply matches the count she wrote and the status she decided.

incremental.description: Correcting an item code when the cabinet label and the supply record disagree.

approvals.approved_version: Supply status for this count, as she confirmed it against the cabinet count. A later change voids the confirmation. This message is not a prescription.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The cabinet count, the status decision, the check and telling the clinic stay at full time. Only the recopied use list, the count-versus-par arithmetic, and the pharmacy message after confirmation shrink, and only when the use log and the par already exist. If the par is a shelf card, the flag stays blank. The 0.6 hour is code mismatches. A witness count required by national rules stays in the count.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Direct or provide home health services for a person at home.

steps.what: Provide the home health service in the person's home.
Direct the family on the home health services given.
Write the visit note of the home health services.
Decide which health services the record must state.
Draft the home health record from the visit note.

loop.input: The visit note from s3 and the services decision from s4. No recording of the home and no diagnosis code.
loop.output: Draft lines of the home health record.
loop.check: Every sentence states only a service the services decision already names, and points at a phrase in the visit note. It adds no service, medicine, dose or diagnosis.
loop.stop: One pass. If any sentence fails the check, the draft stays blank and the nurse writes the record.
loop.why_not_simpler: The visit note is free text. A fixed template cannot phrase what she saw in that home, and a rule cannot tell a supported line from one the note does not state.

steps.what: Check the home health draft against that visit note.
File the confirmed home health record.

tasks.design: She still provides the home health service, directs the family, writes the visit note, and decides what the record must state. A draft in {OTHER}, the electronic patient record, phrases only that note and that decision, and stays blank if a line adds a service, medicine or diagnosis. She confirms the text before {OTHER} stores it. No microphone is used.
tasks.previous_blocker: The home record was typed up afterwards from memory, separate from the note she wrote in the house.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded loop can phrase only a note and a decision she already wrote, and the record can store that text after she confirms it.
tasks.still_hard: The visit, the direction to the family, and a thin note that cannot support a line.
tasks.human_edge: She sees the home and the family, and she refuses a line her visit note does not support.

ambition.what: Every home visit gets a confirmed record the same day, including short visits that used to stay untyped.

tasks.altitude: She still provides the service and directs the family. The week loses the second writing of a record she already noted. Prescription rights do not move.

reach.task: Carry out the care she directed in the home
reach.learn: Follow what she said in the home. An unconfirmed draft is not an instruction.

reach.task: Read the home record before any prescription change
reach.learn: A blank draft is not a diagnosis and not a request to prescribe.

evidence.claim: Autoscriber records the consultation, the clinician validates, and the note can be stored in the patient record.
Across 236,153 generated notes in one European health system, self-estimated time per note fell from 6.69 to 4.72 minutes.
A prescription comes from a named practitioner.
The patient dossier is kept twenty years after the last change.
Providers must know whether a generative tool is a medical device, assess risks, train, test and monitor it.
Ambient recording that captures staff performance needs works-council consent.
Solely automated decisions that significantly affect a person need a stated basis.

assumptions: Providing the service, directing the family, writing the visit note and deciding what the record must state stay at remaining 100. The design does not shorten those steps.

The draft's only inputs are the visit note, produced in s3, and the services decision, produced in s4. She writes the note herself. No microphone records the home. The loop does not read a diagnosis code or a medicine code.
Filing in s7 stores only the confirmed text from s6. A blank draft means she writes the record and the filing step does not run.
This flow does not prescribe. A medicine line appears only when her visit note and her decision already state it. The named practitioner still prescribes.

Where the digest names Dutch rules, dossier retention, the named-practitioner rule and works-council consent for ambient recording apply. This design does not record the home. Elsewhere, national rules apply. The study minutes are not this task's saving.
The 0.8 hour per 100 baseline hours is a monthly sample of filed lines the visit note does not support, plus the rare visit she writes in full because the draft stayed blank.
unknowns: Whether this employer's home records need a physician countersignature before filing.
Whether the works council has already consented to edit logs on home-visit notes.
research_questions: What share of these home visits include a medicine she administered, which the draft must not add unless her note already states it?

already_counted.description: Reading the draft against the visit note and the services decision.

incremental.description: Monthly sample of filed home records for a line the visit note does not support, and the rare full rewrite when the draft stays blank.

approvals.approved_version: Home health record for this visit, as she confirmed it against the visit note. A later change voids the confirmation. This file is not a prescription.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The visit, the direction to the family, the visit note and the decision stay at full time. Only phrasing the formal record from that note, and filing the confirmed text, shrink. Thin notes leave the draft blank, so she writes the record. The 0.8 hour is the monthly sample and those rewrites. The published note-time study is not applied here.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Teach classes on mental health topics such as stress reduction.

steps.what: Decide the class aim for this mental health topic.
Choose the vetted page that matches the mental health topic.
Draft the class outline from the topic aim and that page.

loop.input: The class aim from s1 and the page she chose in s2, including its paragraph text. No patient record.
loop.check: Every sentence quotes the chosen page or the class aim, and adds no health claim the page does not state. It names no patient.
loop.stop: One pass. If any sentence fails the check, or if s2 recorded no page, the outline stays blank and she writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: The page is prose and the aim is free text. A fixed handout cannot match this topic, and a rule cannot tell a quoted line from a claim the page does not make.

steps.what: Check each class sentence against the chosen page.
Release the accepted class outline to the attendees.
Teach the class on mental health topics such as stress reduction.

tasks.design: She still sets the aim, chooses the page, and teaches the class. A draft in {DOCS} phrases the outline only from that page and the aim, and stays blank if a sentence adds a health claim the page does not state. She confirms it before the outline is released. The class itself stays hers.
tasks.previous_blocker: The handout was written from memory, and the class still had to be taught in the room.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded loop can phrase an outline only from a page she chose and an aim she set, after she checks every sentence.
tasks.still_hard: Teaching the room, noticing who is lost, and any personal advice the page does not state.
tasks.human_edge: She reads the room and answers a personal question the page does not cover, in her own words.

ambition.what: Every class outline cites the chosen page, including a short stress-reduction session.

tasks.altitude: She still teaches every class and still chooses the page. The week loses writing the handout from memory. Personal advice stays spoken by her.

reach.task: Teach a later session from the accepted outline
reach.learn: Teach it in person. The outline is not a substitute for the class, and a withdrawn page means the outline stays blank.

reach.task: Load vetted pages before a class is drafted
reach.learn: A page needs an id, a title, the paragraph text and the body that approved it. Without that text the outline stays blank.

evidence.claim: Thuisarts publishes guideline-based information for the public, from the professional bodies and the patient federation.
A person must be told when they are interacting with an AI system.
Providers must know whether a generative tool is a medical device, assess risks, train, test and monitor it.
Solely automated decisions that significantly affect a person need a stated basis.

assumptions: Setting the aim, choosing the page and teaching the class stay at remaining 100. The design does not shorten the class.

The chosen page is produced in s2. Library contract, fields page id, title, paragraph text and approving body. Producer is the guideline owner. A document administrator loads the text before this task. That load is not this task and is not counted as saved. If s2 records no page, the outline stays blank.
The draft uses only the class aim and that page. It names no patient. Personal advice that the page does not state is spoken by her in the class, not written into the outline.
s5 releases only the outline she confirmed in s4. She teaches even when the outline stays blank.
The class is taught by her. This design does not open a channel where attendees talk to the draft. If a later channel did, disclosure would apply.
The 0.6 hour per 100 baseline hours is rewriting an outline when the chosen page is withdrawn before the class.
unknowns: Which vetted pages this service is allowed to quote for mental health classes.
Whether the class is staff-only or open to patients and families.
research_questions: Does this service already keep a list of approved pages for stress-reduction classes?

already_counted.description: Reading each outline sentence against the page she chose.

incremental.description: Rewriting the outline when the chosen page is withdrawn before the class.

approvals.approved_version: Class outline for this topic, quoted from the page she chose, as she confirmed it. A later change voids the confirmation.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The aim, the page choice and the class stay at full time. The outline is drafted only from the chosen page and stays blank when no page fits. The 0.6 hour is a rewrite after a withdrawn page. She still teaches when the handout is blank.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: She still counts the cabinet, provides home services and teaches the class. Confirmed records and outlines keep her wording. A supply message does not prescribe.
reach: Pharmacist: issue stock against the existing par from the confirmed shortage list, and do not treat that list as a prescription.
Home-care worker: follow the direction she gave in the home, not an unconfirmed draft.
Colleague nurse: teach a later class from the accepted outline, in person.
skills_to_grow: Leave a home-record draft blank when the visit note does not support the line.
Reject a class sentence the chosen page does not say.
Mark a supply for the pharmacy only after counting it short and confirming the list.
role.ambitious_version: Each count produces a confirmed status against the pharmacist's par. Each home visit has a record whose lines cite her note. Each class outline quotes a page she accepted. She still counts, visits and teaches.
